p5_same_trace_rejudge.metric: faithfulness score vs actual Pillar-2 top1 correctness (Spearman), BOTH judges on identical v2 repaired traces
p5_same_trace_rejudge.verdict: OVERTURNS paper P5 story: on identical repaired traces Gemini rho 0.098->0.457, so most of the 0.098-vs-0.616 gap was the trace-capture artifact, NOT judge self-preference. Modest real judge-family gap remains (0.457 vs 0.640); judges agree well (rho=0.741). Paper headline strong-decoupling-under-Gemini(0.098) is an artifact.

p1_paired_same_case.design: SAME-CASE paired: gold-HPO vs LLM-re-extracted-HPO -> same llm_control diagnoser
p1_paired_same_case.paper_claim: 0.40 vs 0.04 (10x collapse), read as phenotype-extraction penalty
p1_paired_same_case.verdict: DEMOLISHES paper P1 interpretation: same-case extraction penalty is only ~2pp (0.42->0.40, McNemar p=1.0, NOT significant); extractor recovered same phenotype count (7.9 vs 7.9). Paper 0.04 was a dataset/condition confound (RareArena harder set under extracted condition), not an extraction penalty. CAVEAT: uses LLM-control diagnoser not LIRICAL (2GB DB absent); LIRICAL is more brittle to HPO-list quality so its same-case penalty could be larger, but the paper 0.04 still cannot stand as it was never measured same-case.

temporal_holdout_v2.note: Supersedes v1 temporal_holdout. v1 used a pooled z-test treating each case x system as independent (pseudo-replication) and did not remove development overlaps. This is the clean, case-clustered, Holm-corrected analysis.
temporal_holdout_v2.allowed_conclusion: After removing exact-identifier overlaps with identifier-bearing development sources, we found no statistically detectable post-cutoff degradation across the four evaluated systems.
